issues.description: The solution's Person class declares the first-name field with a different identifier than used by its getters, setters, equals, and hashCode, causing a structural inconsistency and likely compile errors. In the template Person class the field is declared as 'firstName' and all accessors refer to it. In the solution Person class the backing field is declared as 'forename' while the methods still reference 'firstName'. This mismatch in the solution contradicts the template and the intended model and will confuse students when comparing template, tests, and solution or trying to run the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the field name in the solution's Person class consistent with its accessors and with the template. Rename the declared field 'forename' back to 'firstName' (or rename all getters/setters/equals/hashCode to use 'forename') so that the field identifier and all method references match. Ensure the equals and hashCode implementations reference the same field name.

issues.description: The Person entity's first-name attribute is inconsistently named across artifacts: the problem statement and template use the identifier 'firstName' (and corresponding accessor methods setFirstName/getFirstName), while the solution's Person model declares the field as 'forename'. This breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the described domain concept (a person's first name), the template class, and the final solution, creating confusion when reading or modifying the code and when tests/references use setFirstName/getFirstName.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the person's first name across all artifacts. Rename the solution model field 'forename' to 'firstName' and ensure all getters/setters and equals/hashCode use 'firstName', or alternatively update the template/tests/problem to use 'forename' consistently. Prefer matching the template/problem's 'firstName' to minimize changes to tests and exercise text.
